prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary/dispatch/status; Export Limit Advisory when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: approved switching, clearances, escalates alarms, notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped data→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: dispatch target/ramp, keeps last validated limit on grid comms loss. Grid Dispatcher: targets; priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag; schedules updated on confirmed vessel/task changes. Mode Grid Constraint. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale; repair prioritization. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; repair window, records, follow-up; checks task vs work authorization, personnel/equipment. Maintenance starts only after scope, access route, supervisor confirmed. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Storekeeper: materials/tooling, critical spares, marine packaging. Warehouse System: cargo prep before berth. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note. Weather Service (considered with berth availability), Metocean Buoy. Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation→Marine Coordinator. Marine Coordinator: berth view; resolves berth conflicts (urgency, compatibility, delay); resequences lower priority preserving rest/inspections; disruption alternatives (later slot, other berth, standby); records actual times. Vessel Master: Crew Count Correction; confirms arrival/departure vs limits. Work Permit Portal: Isolation Boundary Sketch; reviewed before departure. Redoubt (permit control) blocks release. Personnel Tracking Console reconciled with crew list before boarding; North/South

New part:
S493: The Field Supervisor reviews the worksite limits with the crew before anyone enters the controlled area.
S494: Physical boundaries are marked so that the work area and any adjacent operating equipment are clearly distinguishable.
S495: The crew confirms that the marked limits match the current isolation points and the approved maintenance scope.
S496: The Electrical Technician verifies electrical isolation at the work location before work on electrical equipment begins.
S497: The Substation Operator confirms that switching conditions affecting the worksite are understood by the relevant personnel.
S498: The Vessel Master confirms that the vessel is safely positioned and that transfer conditions remain acceptable.
S499: The Marine Coordinator suspends access when sea or weather conditions make transfer unsafe.
S500: A Weather Hold remains in effect until the responsible operational authority confirms that conditions permit work to proceed.
S501: Personnel use the North Access Scanner or South Access Scanner at the designated entry point.
S502: The Personnel Tracking Console is checked to confirm that people entering and leaving the site are accounted for.
S503: The Field Supervisor verifies each worker's authorization, competence, and fitness for the assigned task.
S504: Before starting, the crew inspects personal protective equipment, communications equipment, and rescue equipment for serviceability.
S505: The HSE Officer checks that emergency routes, muster points, and rescue arrangements are understood by everyone at the worksite.
S506: The crew tests the required radio channel with the Operations Radio Console before separating into work teams.
S507: Tools and loose materials are secured against dropped-object hazards and movement caused by vessel motion.
S508: Access to the worksite is restricted to personnel listed for the task, and visitors remain under escort.
S509: The Field Supervisor pauses the job if actual conditions differ from the approved method or the marked worksite boundaries.
S510: Any change to the work scope requires a renewed safety review before affected work resumes.
S511: The crew maintains clear access to fire equipment, escape routes, and lifting areas throughout the task.
S512: At shift handover, the outgoing supervisor briefs the incoming supervisor on site conditions, access status, and outstanding hazards.
S513: Work is closed out only after personnel are accounted for, equipment is removed or secured, and the worksite is left in a safe condition.
S514: Switching coordination begins with a defined operational need, a safe sequence, and an agreed period for execution.
S515: The Duty Planner develops the proposed sequence with the Control Engineer and identifies affected equipment and operating limits.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
